title: Why Reading/Watching Yuyu Hakusho will make you LEVEL UP
summary: NH recommends Yu Yu Hakusho, a manga he collected over more than ten years and credits with shaping him physically and spiritually. He praises its relatable skinny hero surrounded by jacked characters, mostly physical fights, the villain Toguro, its moral ambiguity, the Dark Tournament arc, and its Nietzschean themes, and recommends the anime over the manga.
claims: It took NH more than 10 years to collect every volume of Yu Yu Hakusho, and he says the series shaped his physical and spiritual development
As a scrawny kid NH related more to the small, imperfect Yusuke than to giant heroes like Goku, which also fits lifters at the start of their journey
The show is a muscle fest with mostly bare-knuckle physical fights rather than magic, appealing to fans of physical showdowns
Watch the anime rather than read the manga: Togashi's art is erratic, and the full anime is on YouTube in HD with a decent English dub and an excellent soundtrack
Toguro, whose power is controlling his own flex like a gym rat with on-demand pumps, is one of the best-written villains in shonen
The story's moral ambiguity between humans and demons, with demons offering compelling justifications, makes it more than a good-versus-evil tale
The Yusuke vs Toguro fight is an ideological battle: might makes right versus strength only having meaning when it protects something dear
Yu Yu Hakusho embodies NH's ideal of 'educated barbarianism', brutal yet intelligent, culminating in Yusuke's Nietzschean evolution and the nihilist villain Sensui
